from: October book, night 8 (A Kind Word for the Weary)
p1: Isaiah wrote some words as if Jesus Himself were talking. Long before Jesus was born, Isaiah knew about Him.
In those words, Jesus says the Lord taught Him how to speak. He would know the right word for someone weary.
Weary means so tired that your body and heart need rest. Every morning, the Lord woke Jesus to listen and learn.
p2: Long ago, people walked far on dusty roads and worked hard all day. A kind word helped a tired heart feel strong again. Jesus said, “Come unto Me, and I will give you rest.”
Your words can help a tired heart too. Tonight, give a hug and a kind word to someone who is tired.
old: Long ago, Heavenly Father's people lived far away from home, in a land called Babylon. They were tired and sad and they missed home. So a prophet named Isaiah — a prophet is someone Heavenly Father teaches — told them about a special helper who would come. Isaiah called Him the Servant, which means someone who comes to help. That Servant is Jesus.

Isaiah said that every morning Heavenly Father would wake Jesus up and teach Him what to say. So Jesus always knew the right gentle word for someone who was tired. A kind word can warm a tired heart, the way a soft blanket warms cold toes.

Isaiah also said Jesus would set His face like flint. Flint is a very hard rock that does not crack or break. Isaiah picked that picture because Jesus would keep going and never give up, even when people were unkind to Him. Jesus could say, "Heavenly Father will help Me."

Then Isaiah asked the sad people a question: "Is anyone walking in the dark with no light?" He did not only mean nighttime. He meant the times when you cannot tell what is coming next. Isaiah told them what to do: trust Heavenly Father and hold on tight to Him, like holding a hand. The dark does not last forever.
Tonight your room will get dark too. You do not need a lamp to be safe. You can whisper Jesus' name, and He is right there with you, with a gentle word just for you.
